title: Ramayana: Part 1 Is Already Racing at the Box Office — Record Advance Bookings and a Court Shield Two Days Before Release
excerpt: Ramayana: Part 1 opens worldwide Nov. 5 with Rs 32.53 crore in day-1 advance bookings, 8.14 lakh tickets sold, and Bombay High Court anti-piracy protection.
content:
Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1 arrives in cinemas worldwide on November 5, 2026, and the advance booking numbers reported on Tuesday, November 3, show a release already moving at blockbuster speed. According to Sacnilk figures reported by Filmibeat, the film had sold 8.14 lakh tickets for its opening day by noon IST on November 3, worth Rs 32.53 crore in advance bookings.

That opening-day presale total puts Ramayana: Part 1 ahead of Ajay Devgn's Drishyam: The Conclusion, whose opening-day presales stood at Rs 31.65 crore, and makes it the second-highest opening-day advance booking of 2026 so far, behind Dhurandhar 2 at Rs 52.35 crore, Filmibeat reported. Advance bookings for the November 5-8 opening weekend were reported at more than Rs 100 crore in total, including more than Rs 60 crore in India and more than Rs 40 crore overseas.

The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, with Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. It is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in association with Monster Mind Creations, and it releases in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam, with dubbing reported in 40 languages worldwide. Its reported budget for Part 1 is Rs 2,000 crore.

Two days before release, the Bombay High Court granted the film protection against piracy. Justice Madhav Jamdar passed a dynamic ad-interim injunction in a commercial suit filed by Godpower Media Private Limited, which holds the film's domestic and territorial intellectual property and exploitation rights. The order restrains unidentified entities from illegally recording, hosting, streaming or distributing the film and its copyrighted material, including its script, character designs, footage, music and lyrics. The matter is scheduled for a further hearing on December 16.

The film's pull on premium screens is already reshaping other releases in India. Godzilla Minus Zero, which opens in Japan on November 3 and in North America on November 6, has had its India release moved to November 20, Sacnilk reported, linked to Ramayana's reported two-week IMAX exclusivity window in India.

Analysis: A release being treated as an event, not just a film

Three things are converging here, and each one raises the stakes for opening weekend. The presale pace says demand is already national, not limited to one language market. The court order says the makers are treating leaks as a release-week threat, not an afterthought. And the IMAX calendar says exhibitors have already bet their best screens on this film for two weeks. If the opening weekend matches the advance bookings, Ramayana: Part 1 will set the standard every other big Indian release this year is measured against. If it falls short, the same numbers will make that shortfall impossible to hide.
